_meta.title: Unaccredited-for-building Alberta municipalities and where building applications go
_meta.method: For each of the 75 municipal-type rows that the A16 inventory (2026-10-25) lists as not accredited for building, one read-only query of the public Safety Codes Council Accreditation Search (the tool behind 'Where to get a Permit'), organization type and discipline left blank, organization name set to the municipality's core name. The search matches substrings across all organization types. Nine baseline searches (all municipalities, municipalities with Building, joint municipalities, regional services commissions, agencies with Building, all agencies, corporations with Building, event location records, DAO) were run first.
_meta.personal_data: The search results include a QMP manager name and e-mail per row. They were not parsed or stored.
_meta.result: All 75 queries agree with the A16 snapshot of 2026-10-25: none of the 75 is accredited for Building under its own name, and no joint municipality or regional services commission whose name contains the municipality's core name is accredited for Building. Own disciplines found: Fire only for 39, none for 36.
limits: The search is not a location lookup. Its fields are organization type, discipline, the organization's own listed city, and organization name. It cannot say which agency serves a project address.
The 'Site List' report linked from each row redirected to a 'Login Required' page when fetched without an account (tested on one row, dl/5). It was not pursued.
Joint-municipality names list member municipalities in free text. Membership was matched by name only.
ASCA's Order covers Building, Electrical, Gas, Plumbing, Private Sewage and storage tank systems. It does not name the Fire discipline other than storage tank systems.

facts.text: ASCA oversees permit-related services for buildings, electrical, gas, plumbing, private sewage and storage tank systems in areas not under the administration of an accredited municipality, regional services commission or corporation.
facts.quote: In the areas of Alberta that are not under the administration of an accredited municipality, an accredited regional services commission or an accredited corporation, the Authority shall oversee the provision of permit-related services
facts.source: Alberta Safety Codes Authority Order, AR 29/2016 s.4(1) (consolidated up to 208/2024)

facts.text: In ASCA areas the owner picks the contracted agency. It is not assigned by area.
facts.quote: ASCA contracts a number of accredited agencies to provide compliance monitoring services throughout the province so you can select a service provider that works for you.
facts.source: Safety Codes Council, Alberta Safety Codes Authority page

facts.text: The agencies page tells owners to weigh distance, familiarity with the community and timing.
facts.quote: Things to consider when choosing your agency service provider: Are they close to your project location? ... Are they familiar with your community? Does their timing work for you?
facts.source: Safety Codes Council, ASCA Contracted Agencies

facts.text: ASCA fees are the same whichever agency the owner contracts.
facts.quote: Standardized permit fees, meaning no matter which agency you contract your permit cost will be the same.
facts.source: Safety Codes Council, Alberta Safety Codes Authority page

facts.text: ASCA has its own safety codes officers who review plans, issue permits and inspect.
facts.quote: Yes, ASCA has its own safety codes officers that provide consultative advice/guidance, plans reviews, issue permits, and conduct inspections.

facts.text: The 'Where to get a Permit' page links to the Accreditation Search, whose fields are Organization Type, Discipline, City and Organization Name.
facts.quote: Click here to find an accredited organization by type, discipline(s), region, or name.
facts.source: Safety Codes Council, Where to get a Permit; Accreditation Search form

facts.text: No page states who issues a variance in an ASCA area. By the Act, an SCO designated with a variance power may issue it: ASCA's own officers or an SCO of the contracted agency, acting for ASCA (IB-2026-10-16).
facts.quote: SCOs exercise delegated powers on behalf of those entities, within their designation and terms of employment.
facts.source: SCC Information Bulletin IB-2026-10-16; Safety Codes Act ss.32, 33(5)-(6), 38
